summary: I re-ran every repro and they reproduce, and I built my own control rather than trusting theirs: a 22,464-cell sweep (CAP_TARGETS x CAP_FAB_START incl. -5/0/12/1843/1844/1845/4095/4096/5000 x CAP_VOCAB_START x CAP_LIFT in {0,0.08,0.5,2.0} x CAP_LIFT_MIN in {0,1,8} x LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS x FAB_SLOTS in {2,10,4096}) against a BEFORE mirror whose api.py is md5 642e74eae8adc14c1572875a9ba0478f == git show HEAD~1. THE CENTRAL CLAIM HOLDS AND IS STRONGER THAN FILED: printed one-lift arithmetics claiming a result ABOVE the ceiling went 16,308 of 22,464 -> 0 of 27,807; every one of the 3,630 'CLAMPED at the ceiling from R' renderings satisfies R > ceiling == printed value; every one of the 15,933 'none, at_hard_ceiling refuses A >= B' has A == cap, B == ceiling and A >= B; no plain lift lowers a cap; ZERO cap.valve or cap.vocab_arm_honest verdict moved on any cell, no gate was lost, no resolved cap changed, and all 13,810 textually-changed cap.valve lines classify into the three clamp edits with NOTHING unaccounted. _clamped_lift's numbers, the 302 sub-ceiling caps (3794..4095, 7 of 9 at FAB_SLOTS=10), the restored-cap 5000 route, the historic 'one lift -> 4422' on a FIRED gate, all four cap.clamp states and every lift_to figure in both files reproduce exactly. BUT I REFUTE THREE THINGS. (1) The new Gate cap.clamp prints a FALSE, SELF-CONTRADICTING sentence on 2,283 of my 22,464 cells: its UNREACHABLE arm says 'no lift can be earned at all on this configuration' and then, in the SAME sentence, 'observe refuses every lift it earns by name as dead_rows_unmasked' (1,692 cells) or 'ONE EARNED LIFT DOES NOT MOVE IT' (627) -- two env vars reach it (CAP_TARGETS=vocab CAP_VOCAB_START=1000). cap.valve, whose predicate it borrows, says 'no armed arm can LIFT'; the new gate is the one that chose 'EARNED', and observe's own docstring says those lifts ARE earned and counted. A false equation printed by the fix meant to end false equations, on the very gate the ruling added. (2) capacity/api.py:37 still reads 'both its Gates are readable' -- there are now THREE, in the file that spells 'EIGHT keys to TEN' twice for exactly this reason (docs/04_CONTRACT.md:1350 carries the same stale count). (3) capacity/levers.py:176-177 asserts 'Measured with K13's own scanner over this file: ONE numeric claim examined before this rewrite and five after' -- I measured it with K13's own _k13_scan: 1 before, SEVEN after; their own summary says 7. The 'five' is the true figure for src/spine/assemble.py (I measured that too: 5), copied without re-measuring -- a count in prose that is a copy of a fact, in the paragraph written to end that. D16 ITSELF IS NARROWER THAN THE HEADLINE: observe is `raise NotImplementedError`, so nothing clamps in a run, no counter is ever incremented and Decision.clamped is never set; the clamp executes only inside new_valve's startup gates. Their unfinished #3 discloses this; the finding headline 'D16 IMPLEMENTED' and the summary do not. Their two docs/04_CONTRACT.md unfinished items are ALREADY LANDED at HEAD and must not be relayed as outstanding. All citations in both files resolve (I opened every one), but two NEW ones are split across a newline and O13's existence half scans line-by-line -- I planted a split citation to a nonexistent symbol and O13 PASSED it VACUOUSLY while the same citation on one line FAILS it.

I re-proved the property the docstring asserts rather than sampling it: with the startup refusal holding frac>=0 and floor>=0, derive.lift_to (`int(cap) + max(int(floor), int(frac*cap))`) is >= int(cap) on EVERY input, so max(int(cap), min(lift_to, hard)) >= int(cap) always. The restored-cap route builds and renders as filed.

findings.detail: THE RULING IS RECORDED, THE MECHANISM DOES NOT RUN, AND THE HEADLINE DOES NOT SAY SO. observe's body is `cap = cap.owned_by('CAP')` then `raise NotImplementedError`, so nothing in a run applies _clamped_lift, no lift is ever clamped, cap.lifts_clamped_experts/_vocab are seeded at 0 and never incremented, and Decision.clamped is never set by any code that exists. The ONLY executing callers of _clamped_lift are new_valve's _lift_moves and _one_lift, i.e. the startup Gate lines. That is the correct state for a frozen-contract package and their unfinished item #3 says so precisely -- but the finding is titled 'D16 IMPLEMENTED' and the summary says 'D16 ... is implemented as CLAMP', which a supervisor can relay to the owner as 'the valve now clamps'. It does not; it will when P4 writes observe. The interpretation question the ruling actually turned on IS answered on the record: reading (ii) is stated in observe's docstring with the three grounds, and I checked each against the tree -- Valve declares exactly FOURTEEN fields and none is a clamp flag; CAP.state's declared payload is 'The lifted caps AND the two pin clocks AND the high-water marks' and nothing else; observe's per-flush inputs carry no ceiling and no demand level. Reading (ii) is the reading a careful person gives those words on THIS mechanism, since 'released ... goes down' would require lowering a cap, which the module's founding sentence and the CAP_LIFT/CAP_LIFT_MIN startup refusal both forbid.

findings.detail: THE FOUR STATES RENDER AS FILED -- I reproduced all four, the ledger really goes from eight keys to ten, and the two counters are seeded at 0 -- BUT THE CLAIM THAT 'THE FOURTH STATE IS NOT SMUGGLED' AND THAT 'UNREACHABLE = no lift can be earned at all' IS FALSE ON 2,283 OF MY 22,464 CELLS, AND IT IS FALSE IN THE SAME PRINTED SENTENCE. _clamp_gate's unreachable arm opens with 'no lift can be earned at all on this configuration' and then splices in cap.valve's `dead` sentences, two of which assert the opposite: (a) 1,692 cells print '... no lift can be EARNED at all ...: the vocabulary arm has room to earn (1000 against a hard ceiling of 4096) and LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=False, so observe refuses every lift IT EARNS by name as dead_rows_unmasked'; (b) 627 cells print '... no lift can be EARNED at all ...: the expert arm's soft cap is 12 and ONE EARNED LIFT DOES NOT MOVE IT'. This is not a wording quibble in this tree: observe's own docstring says dead_rows_unmasked 'counts precisely the lifts that were EARNED and then refused for dishonesty, which is a number no other line in the run carries', so under the contract those flushes increment the histogram while this gate says none can exist -- and in case (b) observe would take a lift of size 0 on every flush, so CAP.counters' lifts_experts climbs while cap.clamp prints UNREACHABLE and '0 lift(s) taken'. cap.valve, whose reachability predicate this gate deliberately borrows, is careful here: it says 'no armed arm can LIFT'. The new gate is the one that reached for 'EARNED', which is the one word that makes it false. Reachable with TWO environment variables.
